extracted.intended_audience: readers and historians of early American Catholic missions; members/administrators of the Loretto community
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted directives and prescriptive passages from Father Nerinckx's will and letters: bequests, procedural wishes about property and funds, and exhortations for the Loretto Sisters' conduct and missionary practice in early-19th-century American Catholic contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of utensil-sale funds for clergy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is his desire that this money should go toward paying the expenses of a clergyman from over the sea for Kentucky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original context: 'The utensils at the new place ... he paid two hundred dollars for, a sum they may be worth now. It is his desire that this money should go toward paying the expenses of a clergyman from over the sea for Kentucky.' Also mentions he received five hundred guilders (≈$180) for that purpose which was not complied with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of Miss Du Moulin's gift (700 guilders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven hundred guilders ... for an anniversary in the Loretto chapel, or for some Masses, founded at her intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Father notes the donor's probable intention was to assist religion in America; 'This foundation is not made; but he said some Masses, and some solemn ones have been celebrated. Both these matters are left to stand as they are: it belongs to the Bishop to fix them.' Authority for final decision is the Bishop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of debts/receivables for local houses
rubrics_metrics.description: The congregations now in Rev. Mr. Abel's care owe him $25.75 ... If there be any sisters sent to Union county, as the Bishop said, they may have this money. Charles Vessel's ten dollars and George Thompson's debts are for Loretto. Thomas Cecil's forty dollars will give twenty dollars to Loretto, ten for Gethsemani, and ten for Calvary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific allocations of small outstanding debts/loans to be distributed among named nunneries or missions as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of potential future salaries for benefit of orphans
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the congregations once under his care ever be moved to pay him salaries, they may be divided among the nunneries for the benefit of the orphans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction to redirect any future remuneration to nunneries/orphan care rather than to the writer personally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clothing and personal belongings bequeathed to orphans (Loretto priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: If tidings arrive that he is dead, or does not return, his clothes, linen, pictures, and English boots, as far as useful, are for the orphans of the schools, savingly and sparingly to be made use of. Loretto having to take care of the greatest number, must have the greatest share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference explicitly given to Loretto because of numbers in their care; items to be used sparingly and for school orphans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and location of church apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: The church apparatus, viz., chalices, vestments, etc., he desires to remain as they are and where they are at present. The bells of Loretto never to be removed, nor the pictures. The little chalice his brother of London gave him, and now at Mr. James Dent's, is only lent to him; it may remain there his lifetime, if no more urgent call comes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear instruction to keep sacred objects and church fittings in situ; specific exception for a loaned chalice (temporary, removable under urgent need).

rubrics_metrics.name: Library preservation and restricted use
rubrics_metrics.description: The books at Loretto ought to be kept unmolested, and the little library may be at the service of the reverend gentleman who has the care of Loretto, only; best care to be taken of them, but never to become his property, not even to change them for others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books must not be dispersed or treated as personal property of caretakers; caretaker may use them but must preserve and not exchange them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall executor/custodian recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole recommended to the care of the Right Rev. Bishop Flaget, or his successor in the See of Bardstown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Father designates episcopal authority (Bishop Flaget or successor) as ultimate custodian and decision-maker for the matters in his will; procedural guidance for implementation rests with the Bishop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict observance of Loretto society rules and evangelical virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: He begs ... that the members of the Loretto Society and particularly of the House of Loretto, should ever study their rules — never make any the least infraction in them. Poverty and humility of Jesus and Mary; obedience and chastity of Jesus and Mary; union, peace, and concord of Jesus and Mary; zeal for souls ... Gain souls, hunt souls, catch souls, court souls, draw souls, pull souls, carry souls, deliver souls, shelter souls, buy souls! ... Souls! souls! and nothing but souls, for the love of Jesus, the owner of all souls!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A programmatic exhortation establishing the society's priorities and behavioral standards: strict rule-following, embrace poverty/humility/obedience/chastity/union/peace/concord, and an uncompromising focus on evangelization ('souls and nothing but souls'). Also repeated cultural prescriptions: 'Loretto houses, Loretto dresses, Loretto labors, Loretto hardships, Loretto food, Loretto furniture, Loretto sisters, Loretto scholars' — i.e., preserve Loretto identity and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve institutional identity and material culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Loretto houses, Loretto dresses, Loretto labors, Loretto hardships, Loretto food, Loretto furniture, Loretto sisters, Loretto scholars! Every house on the place Loretto house! Stick to the tree that Mary planted there!... Stick to the dress that Mary gave there!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong prescription to maintain original institutional forms, dress, labor practices, furnishings, and rituals — an anti-change stance aimed at preventing 'degeneration' from the founder's intended communal way of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical travel caution: avoid unknown animals/objects
rubrics_metrics.description: The polecat ... taught us not to interfere with unknown things, and to keep away from them even when their appearance charms us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical safety guideline for travelers/missionaries: do not attempt to handle or provoke unfamiliar animals or phenomena; anecdotal justification (severe odor and lasting contamination) given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising tactic: use admired artifacts to stimulate subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The architect ... placed [the clock] in the front wall of the church ... The people acknowledged that so beautiful a clock should adorn a steeple, and they consented to a subscription, which realized enough to complete the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of a practical fundraising strategy: display or associate a valued/beautiful item publicly to inspire community contributions (symbolic adornment to encourage subscriptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion procedural step: suspension/separation pending dispensation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vicar-general ... advised Mr. Noble to separate from his wife until the necessary dispensation would be obtained from Rome. The really noble convert complied forthwith ... In about six months the dispensation arrived ... the Vicar-general was requested by both husband and wife to receive them into the church, and join them in the holy bonds of a lawful marriage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes a procedural requirement in certain conversions: where impediments to reception exist (e.g., marriage irregularities), temporary separation and obtaining a dispensation from Rome may be required before reception into the Church and regularization of marriage; emphasizes willingness to comply as part of conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionary instruction and baptism practice (practical pastoral guideline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Father Rosati ... instructed an Indian chief carefully for several days ... Having given him an instruction about baptism, the Indian immediately signified his intense desire to receive the sacrament ... the priest delayed no longer, and administered to him that most necessary of sacraments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates a pastoral approach: provide careful, sufficient instruction and, when the catechumen shows readiness and desire, proceed with baptism promptly; the narrative also records the powerful pastoral/evangelical effects and community response.
